notes: One typescript sheet with pen additions, carrying the handwritten manuscript number “- 5 -” and the archival number 69. No title or date appears. It contains fourteen typed correction/reference entries addressing pages 11–17, two handwritten additional entries, an appended handwritten reference, and two displayed identities with pen-written psi signs. The author asks for a reference in Exp.V; wonders whether connectedness of C alone would preserve the definitions; asks SGA or EGA for a known assertion; calls attention to an uncited connected-curve assertion; asks whether “propre et lisse” is sufficient; and questions the inference of smoothness for an X not assumed flat. These are the page’s claims and doubts, not verified results. The final sentence stops after “ne sont pas”, without a final punctuation mark. H supplies only a description and is unavailable as a transcription: every decision has h_reading=null and diff_h=false, and no descriptive omission is counted. The unusual typed single-n form “canule” is confirmed without normalization. The two lowered point indices and the separator after “on trouve” remain explicit C doubts. New in-place uncertainties concern the dash/point separator and final-point writing state in the added reference, and the assignment of the extra low point by the closing quotation after “trouve”. The three class subscripts are read as typewritten chi impressions; their serifed shape could be a composite typewriter construction, but no readable cancelled underlying l is asserted. No proof, computation or external background check was performed.
math_reading_decisions: Confirmed from the upper half: K^{\bullet}(T) versus K_{\bullet}(T). Each K has one upright and two arms, each T one upright and top bar; the marks on K are filled points, raised in the first occurrence and lowered in the second. No double alphabet is inferred.
Confirmed the ordinary single-outline C in the two prose conditions, S in the two relevant entries, and both X occurrences in the p.16, li.16 entry. None shows independent double striking.
The typed exposé V in Exp.V, the typed EGA IV, and the final typed V are ordinary Roman capitals without the separate upper and lower rules seen in the handwritten IV and III.
Confirmed all line and section numbers from the ink, including 3.1, 2.8, 7.13.6, V 6.5.3 and 6.6.4. The only new numerical separator doubt is in the handwritten added reference after trait.

Both displayed psi letters are handwritten: a freely curved upper bowl is crossed by a long central descending stroke. The lower indices i and i+j are typed. The shape is psi rather than phi; no closed circular bowl is present.

Display (i), checked symbol by symbol: \psi_i(c^i(x)) = (-1)^{i-1}(i-1)!c^i_{\chi}(x), with an i exponent on each c, the exponent i-1 on (-1), a factorial after the parenthesized i-1, and a separate terminal comma. These are reading checks only.

Display (ii), checked symbol by symbol: \psi_{i+j}(c^i(x)c^j(y)) = (-1)^{i+j-1}(i+j-1)!c^i_{\chi}(x)c^j_{\chi}(y), with j (a dotted descender) in the second c power and i+j where written. No product dot or extra sign is inserted.

All three lowered class signs read as chi from their crossing strokes; their typewritten appearance, rather than C’s handwritten classification, is recorded separately in decisions B070-11 through B070-13.
The paired x indices remain explicitly uncertain as o|0 and l|1. Their mathematical pairing has not been used to resolve the ink.

No arrow, inequality, commutative diagram, independent drawing, grouping bracket, underlined prose, or deleted passage is present on this page. The Roman-numeral rules are retained as notation. No mathematical assertion has been proved or externally checked.
